name: the Miramare park
title: Ancient Trees in the Miramare Park, Trieste: 6 to Find
meta_description: A Habsburg archduke planted this park on bare Adriatic rock in 1856 to find out what would survive. Six of the trees did, half of them Californian.
intro:
The man who planted these trees was shot by a firing squad in Mexico eleven years later. Archduke Maximilian of Habsburg began the Miramare park in the spring of 1856 on a limestone headland with almost no soil on it, and he ran the whole thing as an experiment: he wanted to know which foreign species would hold on to bare Adriatic rock. The soil was carted in.

The answer is still standing. Six of the trees we map grow here and half of them are Californian: a coast redwood and a Monterey cypress both over four metres round, and a ghost pine whose needles sit so thinly on the branch that you can see the sky through its crown. The thickest trunk here belongs to a holm oak at 5.2 metres, and two official surveys cannot agree on whether it is one trunk or three. The park is free and open daily. Only the castle charges admission.
